title: Reference data backend: tenant list CRUD/disable/reorder per list type with guarded statuses
objective: Port the tenant-scoped reference-data API: CRUD, disable, and reorder per list type (request channels, product lines, cover types, segments, industries, regions, party types, lead/quote statuses, lost reasons, broker types) with guarded-status invariants and historical resolvability of disabled values (P-04, section 12 Settings).
scope: Reference-data endpoints per list type mirroring the reference API (list, create, update, disable/enable, reorder)

Guards: lead/quote statuses keep reporting_category (Open/Quoted/Won/Lost/Expired/Withdrawn), canonical_key, is_terminal; terminal/canonical statuses cannot be disabled or category-reassigned per reference rules
Cover types belong to a product line (dependency enforced); request channels carry the broker flag
Disabled values remain resolvable for historical records (no delete); tenant isolation on every operation
implementation_details: Single domains/reference-data module with a list-type registry (typed discriminator) driving shared handlers plus per-type validation extensions — mirror the .NET ReferenceData endpoints' paths and DTOs.
Reorder endpoint: accepts ordered ids, persists sort_order transactionally.
Validation via zod: name required, uniqueness per tenant+list_type (case rules per reference), broker-flag only for channels, product-line FK for cover types.
Status guards enforced in service layer + DB constraints from T-004; violations return the reference error codes.
Every query tenant-predicated; disabled items filtered from active lists but included with includeDisabled per reference API params.

unit: List-type registry: per-type validation rules (broker flag, product-line dependency, guarded statuses) — pure rule checks
integration: CRUD + reorder per representative list types; uniqueness per tenant enforced; tenant B cannot see/modify tenant A values (403/404)
Disabling a terminal status rejected; disabling a normal value keeps it resolvable on historical records
Cover type with wrong product line rejected; audit rows written for changes
e2e: Settings reference-data spec adapted in T-043

ZOD FIX CONFIRMED GENUINE, TWICE OVER: the trap reproduced empirically against zod 4.4.3 (z.number().nullish().refine(v=>v!=null) parses undefined successfully - the refinement short-circuits on undefined though it DOES run on null); mutant M9 reverted productLineId to the optionalId.refine trap form -> red at exactly 'rejects a cover type with no product line at all' (the test discriminates schema-message from service-message, so the bypass cannot hide behind the shared 422); mutant M9b did the same to reportingCategory -> 2 red ('no reporting category' AND 'not a category at all'). CODEBASE SWEEP FOR THE SAME PATTERN: every .refine site in src/server audited; NO other latent hole. tenants/schemas.ts:51 (contactEmail nullish+refine) and both includeDisabled/includeRemoved query schemas have refinements that PERMIT undefined, so a short-circuit is behaviorally identical (verified empirically: missing param still yields false through the transform); me.schemas.ts themePreference applies refine BEFORE .nullable().optional(), so null/undefined correctly mean 'leave alone'; all remaining refines sit on required strings. RULING 1 (listType parsed-but-unused in update/disable lookup - PRESERVE AS-IS IS CORRECT): consistent with T-016's removed-tenant GET ruling, and NOT the T-013 uniform-denial class, because the quirk contradicts no acceptance criterion and is not an information oracle: the tenant predicate applies (M2 kill proves it), reference_data.manage is one permission across all list types so no privilege is gained by the wrong-listType route, and - decisive - every guard and the duplicate-name check derive from the STORED row's list type (service.ts:189,193), so PUT /region/{statusId} still enforces status rules; the quirk is pure addressing looseness with zero invariant impact, and tightening would 404 currently-200 requests (contract regression under A-3/AC-095 for no security gain). Documented in repository.ts findItem and carried to the T-043/T-044 contract review. RULING 2 (.strict() write schemas + validated reorder bodies - ACCEPTABLE DIVERGENCES): the reorder change replaces a reference NullReferenceException 500 with a 422 - a defect fix, not a contract anyone can rely on; .strict() only changes behavior for clients sending unknown keys, and the SPA verifiably sends exactly the four schema keys (ReferenceDataTab.tsx:333-338 checked first-hand; undefined fields drop in JSON); note zod strips unknown keys even without .strict(), so the smuggling defence was already present - .strict() adds loud rejection, aligned with CLAUDE.md zero-trust input validation. Both are flagged, not silently absorbed, satisfying AC-095's rule; they MUST appear in the consolidated deviation ledger at T-043/T-044 alongside the includeDisabled 422-vs-400 (which follows the T-016-approved includeRemoved precedent). V-047 SCOPE HONESTY CONFIRMED, NOT CREDITED: the task file's unmapped_dotnet_behaviour records that the lead-fetch/dashboard half of V-047 cannot be exercised before lead/dashboard/report endpoints exist; the reference-data half IS covered (disabled rows stay in-table, returned with includeDisabled=true, excluded from pickers, cover type keeps resolving a disabled product line). AUDIT (AC-024/V-031): all four actions assert through the shared exactly-one helper with before/after payloads, plus negative assertions (terminal refusal writes no row; idempotent second disable writes no second row); mutation-audit atomicity is one transaction, strictly stronger than the reference's write-after-SaveChanges. SECURITY: no findings - parameterized queries throughout (the one raw fragment binds its parameter), ids constrained to positive safe integers with routing-404 semantics, fail-closed actorFrom (500 refusing an unscoped query if tenant context is missing), GET-membership-only matches the measured reference fix, no DELETE path exists, nothing sensitive logged. surface: GET  /api/v1/settings/reference-data/{listType}?includeDisabled= - tenant membership only (no permission), per ReferenceDataEndpoints.cs:31 and its 2026-07-13 fix note.
First TENANT-SCOPED surface in the port: /api/v1/settings is not on GLOBAL_ROUTE_PREFIXES, so the T-013 middleware requires a verified X-Tenant-Id on every route here.
error_mapping_measured: REFERENCE_DATA_NOT_FOUND -> 404; VALIDATION_FAILED / DUPLICATE_NAME / PRODUCT_LINE_REQUIRED / INVALID_PRODUCT_LINE / REPORTING_CATEGORY_REQUIRED / INVALID_INTERMEDIATE_CATEGORY / CANONICAL_FIELDS_IMMUTABLE / REORDER_SET_MISMATCH / TERMINAL_STATUS_CANNOT_BE_DISABLED -> 422 (ReferenceDataEndpoints.cs:115-135).
These problems DO carry a code extension and a detail of 'CODE: message' (:130-135) - the opposite of the Tenant Manager mapper, which omits both. Both are measured, not house style.
Unparseable {listType} -> 400 with the message inline and NO code extension (:107-108). REFERENCE_DATA_INVALID_LIST_TYPE is dead in the reference and is not emitted.
guards: Terminal status cannot be disabled - checked before the already-disabled short-circuit, as the reference orders it.
Canonical status reporting_category is immutable; canonical_key and is_terminal are unreachable from any request shape (write schemas are .strict()).
Non-canonical lead/quote statuses restricted to reporting_category open|quoted on BOTH create and every update.

Cover types require an ACTIVE product line in the same tenant - this is also AC-036's server-side half: a disabled product line is rejected for new/edited cover types while staying resolvable for existing ones.
Disable is the only removal path; there is no delete function in the repository and no DELETE route.
deviations_from_reference: Reorder body shape is validated (422 REFERENCE_DATA_VALIDATION_FAILED) where the reference had no validator and would NullReferenceException into a 500 on a missing orderedIds.
Unparseable ?includeDisabled= answers 422 through the validation path where ASP.NET's bool binder produced a 400 - identical treatment to the T-016 Tenant Manager port's ?includeRemoved=.
Each mutation and its audit row share ONE transaction; the reference wrote the audit row after SaveChangesAsync, so a crash between them lost the trail. Strictly stronger.

Write schemas are .strict() (unknown body keys rejected) where ASP.NET silently ignored them. The SPA sends exactly the four allowed keys (ReferenceDataTab.tsx:333-338), so no client behaviour changes; the benefit is that canonicalKey/isTerminal cannot be smuggled.
Reorder audit row records before/after ordered id lists; the reference audited only the new OrderedIds.
ported_as_is_and_flagged: UPDATE and DISABLE address an item by id ALONE - the route's {listType} is parsed and validated but never used in the lookup (ReferenceDataEndpoints.cs:69,83; UpdateItemCommand.cs:13). So PUT /settings/reference-data/region/{id} where {id} is a broker type edits the broker type. Not a security issue (the tenant predicate still applies, so only the caller's own rows are reachable) but a contract quirk. Tightening it would turn currently-200 requests into 404s, so it is preserved.
Created items always get display_order 0, so a new value sorts to the head of the list until the tenant reorders. Reference behaviour (CreateItemCommandHandler.cs:69).
Duplicate-name checks ignore is_active, so a DISABLED value still reserves its name. Matches both the reference and uq_reference_items_tenant_list_name, which has no partial predicate.
unmapped_dotnet_behaviour: FluentValidation's exact default English message text for the two Name rules could not be measured - no .NET test asserts it, and the messages were framework defaults rather than literals in the source. The error CODE and HTTP status (the parts any client can branch on) are preserved exactly; the wording for those two rules is this port's, in the same shape the T-016 tenants port used.

V-047's 'a lead referencing a disabled value still displays it on lead fetch and in dashboard/report responses' cannot be exercised here: there are no lead, dashboard or report endpoints yet (T-022+). The reference-data half IS covered (disabled values stay in the table, stay returned with includeDisabled=true, and a cover type keeps resolving its product line after that line is disabled). The lead-fetch half must be asserted by the owning task.
decisions_taken_without_explicit_guidanc: Named the buildApp slot `referenceData` and added a matching eighth pin to tests/integration/auth-wiring.test.ts, verified by deleting the wiring line from each root in turn.

Put the error factories in a new errors.ts rather than inlining them in service.ts - mirrors tenants/errors.ts. That is one file beyond the task file's original `files` list; the list above has been updated.

Reorder writes display_order with one UPDATE per id inside the operation's transaction rather than a single CASE expression: the loop is boring, the transaction makes it atomic, and reference lists are tens of rows, not thousands.

mutation_testing.defect_found_by_the_same_discipline: Not a mutation, but found the same way: asserting the reference's validation MESSAGE (not merely the 422) exposed a real schema defect - 'z.number().nullish().refine(v => v != null)' never runs, because zod short-circuits optional schemas on undefined. A cover type with no productLineId and a status with no reportingCategory both bypassed the schema and were caught one layer down by the service, returning the WRONG error code. Fixed by making the conditional fields required-and-typed. A status-code-only test would have passed.
